artifact: Runtime resilience v2 clean-checkout raw-hash drift

overall.one_line_summary: A detached clean Windows checkout of committed repair bytes changed five raw-hashed runtime-v2 sources from LF to CRLF and produced seven deterministic P2 report drifts.
strengths: Three of four clean-checkout portability and path regressions passed.
The failing projection test identified every drifted repository-local output.
Direct diff and SHA-256 comparison isolated the defect to five newly added raw-hashed sources.
weaknesses: The new runbook, profile, envelope, campaign revision, and archive manifest lacked explicit byte-preservation attributes.
The source worktree passed because its files retained LF bytes, while a fresh Windows checkout normalized them to CRLF.
Cleanup and measured-worktree creation remain blocked until a fresh committed checkout passes.

strengths: The detached worktree tested the exact committed bytes and deterministic renderer used for closeout.
A fresh checkout after adding -text must reproduce the source SHA-256 values and pass all four regressions.
The defect affects engineering provenance bytes only and changes no measured counter or scientific conclusion.
The seven report drifts resolve to five exact raw-hash binding changes.
weaknesses: Source-worktree report checks alone could not establish checkout portability.

strengths: The failed disposable-checkout result is retained before cleanup.

weaknesses: The committed repair did not yet satisfy the explicit clean-checkout acceptance criterion.
suggestions: Apply -text only to the five raw-hashed v2 sources and rerun the detached checkout regression on a new committed tip.

findings.observation: Five sources had no text attribute and received CRLF checkout normalization on Windows.
findings.reasoning: Reports expose their raw SHA-256 values, so checkout-dependent line endings make the committed projection non-reproducible.
findings.suggestion: Mark the five exact sources -text and validate from a fresh detached checkout.

questions_for_owner: No new Owner gate is required; the repair is repository-only byte preservation.
